question.text:
$\qquad$ $P(x):$ $x \in \mathbb {N}$ $\qquad$ $Q(x):$ $x \in \mathbb {Z}$

Consider the predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ above. Which of the following expresses the conditional predicate $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x)?$

  1. If $x \in \mathbb {Z},$ then $x \in \mathbb {N}$
  2. $x \in \mathbb {Z}$ if $x \in \mathbb {N}$
  3. $x \in \mathbb {N}$ implies $x \in \mathbb {Z}$
  4. $x \in \mathbb {N}$ only if $x \in \mathbb {Z}$
question.explanation:
Let's recall the following grammatical constructions for the implication $P\Rightarrow Q{:}$

  • If $P,$ then $Q$

  • $P$ only if $Q$

  • $Q$ if $P$

  • $P$ implies $Q$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

  • Option I reads \[ \textbf{if}\quad \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {Z}$}}_{Q(x)}, \quad\textbf{then}\quad \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {N}$}}_{P(x)} \] which corresponds to $Q(x) \Rightarrow P(x).$ $\:{\color{red}\times}$

  • Option II reads \[ \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {Z}$}}_{Q(x)} \quad\textbf{if}\quad \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {N}$}}_{P(x)} \] which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{darkgreen}\checkmark}$

  • Option III reads \[ \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {N}$}}_{P(x)} \quad\textbf{implies}\quad \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {Z}$}}_{Q(x)} \] which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{darkgreen}\checkmark}$

  • Option IV reads \[ \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {N}$}}_{P(x)} \quad\textbf{only if}\quad \underbrace{\textrm{$x \in \mathbb {Z}$}}_{Q(x)} \] which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{darkgreen}\checkmark}$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II, III and IV only."

  • $S$ is sufficient for $N$

  • For $N,$ it is sufficient that $S$

  • $N$ is necessary for $S$

  • For $S,$ it is necessary that $N$

With that in mind, let's examine the given options.

  • Option I reads \[ \underbrace{\textrm{$6 \, | \, x$}}_{P(x)} \quad\textbf{is sufficient for}\quad \underbrace{\textrm{$3 \, | \, x$}}_{Q(x)} \] which corresponds to $P(x) \Rightarrow Q(x).$ $\:{\color{green}\checkmark}$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II and IV only."
